content: On December 22, 2021, emergency use authorization was granted for the treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults who are at high risk of progressing to severe disease, including hospitalization or death. The recommended dosage is 800 mg taken orally every 12 hours for 5 days. Treatment should begin as soon as possible after a COVID-19 diagnosis and within 5 days of symptom onset. Completing the full 5-day course of treatment and adhering to public health isolation guidelines is critical to maximize viral clearance and reduce transmission. If a patient is hospitalized due to severe or critical COVID-19 after starting molnupiravir, the decision to complete the 5-day treatment course is at the discretion of the healthcare provider. Pregnancy status must be verified in females of childbearing potential before initiating treatment. The safety and efficacy of molnupiravir have not been fully established. Reported side effects include diarrhea (2%), nausea (1%), and dizziness (1%). Prescribers or their designees are required to report all serious adverse events and medication errors potentially related to the drug within 7 calendar days of the event's onset. The FDA recommends using FDA Form 3500 for such reports. Animal reproduction studies suggest that molnupiravir may cause fetal harm when administered to pregnant individuals. If used during pregnancy, healthcare providers must communicate the known and potential benefits and risks to the patient. Molnupiravir is not recommended during pregnancy unless the prescribing provider determines that the benefits outweigh the risks for the individual patient. If prescribed during pregnancy, the provider must document that the risks and benefits were discussed with the patient. There is no available human data on the use of molnupiravir in pregnant individuals to assess the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Healthcare providers must provide patients or caregivers with an electronic or hard copy of the “Fact Sheet for Patients and Caregivers” before administering molnupiravir and document that this information was provided. Limited clinical data are available, and serious or unexpected adverse events may occur that have not yet been reported. There is no data on the presence of molnupiravir or its metabolites in human breast milk. However, NHC, a metabolite of molnupiravir, was detected in the plasma of nursing pups from lactating rats treated with the drug. It is unknown whether molnupiravir affects breastfed infants or milk production. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment and for 4 days after the final dose. Providers should consider advising patients to interrupt breastfeeding and pump and discard breast milk during treatment and for 4 days after the last dose. In summary, molnupiravir is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding due to potential risks.
